verdict.rationale: Codegen provides agent-permission settings (control over PR creation, signed commit requirements, rule auto-detection, mention-only response mode) and pause/resume controls on agent runs, which give some coarse-grained control over agent autonomy. However, there is no evidence of distinct tiered autonomy levels (e.g., read-only vs. suggest vs. auto-execute) that an engineering-lead can configure as a graduated scale — settings appear to be individual binary toggles rather than a tiered system. Missing for 10: explicit multi-tier autonomy levels/presets, granular per-action confirmation thresholds, and any documentation framing permissions as a tiered oversight system rather than isolated toggles.
